title: Using AI to Trade Earnings Announcements
author: SnowSilent7695
selftext:
I'm a long-term investor, but have always been curious about making short-term plays around earnings announcements. I built a model that predicts earnings volatility for upcoming announcements and made a Claude/ChatGPT integration to make it interactive and free-flowing e.g. "predict earnings volatility for small and mid-cap stocks in the energy and industrial sectors."

Definitely like it so far, and here's a live demo on Claude that uses the integration to pull a few predictions as well as fully formed research reports on a few names.

If anyone wants to kick the tires, you can test it out in a few ways (free to use and experiment with):

1. Claude: Customize > Add custom connection > in remote server url paste [https://mcp.flexreportfinapi.com/mcp](https://mcp.flexreportfinapi.com/mcp)
2. Claude Code: Open a terminal > `claude mcp add --transport http flexreport` [`https://mcp.flexreportfinapi.com/mcp`](https://mcp.flexreportfinapi.com/mcp) \> /mcp > select Flexreport Finance

comments.author: VesperaAmbrose
comments.body:
Earnings announcements are one of the few events where AI has a real edge, if you can get the data fast enough and execute before the crowd reacts.

The challenge isn't just parsing the announcement; it's modeling the volatility window and sizing positions dynamically based on sentiment + historical move patterns. Most retail algos either over-leverage or hesitate too long.

I've been testing Rift's AI copilot for event-driven setups like this. It monitors earnings calendars 24/7, generates trade ideas with risk parameters pre-calculated, and can auto-execute if you trust the model. The backtesting engine lets you stress-test strategies against past earnings seasons before going live.

Worth exploring if you're serious about systematic earnings plays: [https://rift.ai](https://rift.ai/)
